sentences.text:
Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act,
 1894 (for short "the Act of 1894") was published in 2005.

The Special  ::: Uploaded on - 12/04/2024 ::: Downloaded on - 27/
 ppn 2 53.wp-3870.23.doc Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO) declared his award on 4 th January 2007 and granted compensation @ Rs.1,11,100/- per hector.
4. Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation as granted, the appellant preferred a reference under Section 18 of the Act of 1894.
He sought additional compensation @ Rs.3,06,00,000/- per hector along with other benefits.
The reference proceedings were opposed by the Acquiring Body.
Before the Reference Court, the appellant failed to lead any evidence, as a result of which, on 18 th December 2019, the evidence of the appellant was closed.
The respondents did not lead any evidence.

5. By the judgment dated 1st January 2020, the Reference Court held that the appellant had failed to prove that the market value of the acquired land was greater than the amount of compensation awarded by the SLAO.
The Reference Petition, therefore, came to be dismissed.
Being aggrieved, the appellant has filed the present appeal seeking enhancement in amount of compensation.

6. Shri Hrishikesh Shinde, learned counsel for the appellant Bharatkumar Vishnudas Bhutada Through ... vs The Executive Engineer, And Ors on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22724982/
2 submitted that the appellant had assigned the conduct of the present proceedings to his Power of Attorney holder.
The said Power of Attorney
ppn 3 53.wp-3870.23.doc holder failed to take timely steps to prosecute the reference application.
As a result, the appellant was precluded from leading evidence before the Reference Court and seeking enhancement in the amount of compensation.
According to him, the compensation offered by the SLAO was lower than the market value of the acquired land and grave prejudice would be caused if the amount of compensation is not enhanced.
He therefore, submitted that an opportunity be granted to the appellant to lead evidence before the Reference Court so as to consider the grant of enhanced compensation.
It was submitted that by imposing appropriate conditions, such opportunity would be granted.
7. Shri Sachin Gite, learned counsel appearing for respondent no.1 opposed the aforesaid submissions.
According to him, the Reference Court had granted sufficient opportunity to the appellant to lead evidence.
Since the appellant failed to remain present for leading evidence, his side was closed on 18 th December 2019.
The Reference Court rightly found that there was no material on record to enhance the amount of compensation from that granted by SLAO.
Since there was no illegality committed by the Reference Court, the appeal was liable to be dismissed.

Without prejudice to the aforesaid, it was submitted that in case an opportunity is granted to the appellant, an appropriate order Bharatkumar Vishnudas Bhutada Through ... vs The Executive Engineer, And Ors on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22724982/

In the light of the aforesaid submissions, the following point arises for determination :-
 (i) Whether an opportunity deserves to be granted to the  appellant to seek enhancement in the amount of  compensation ?
9.
We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and with their assistance, we have perused the judgment of the Reference Court.
10. The land of the appellant admeasuring 4 H 99 R is the subject matter of the acquisition.
In the proceedings under Section 18 of the Act of 1894, the appellant sought enhancement in the amount of compensation.
The burden to prove the fact that the market value of the acquired land was more than what was offered by the SLAO was on the appellant.
However, despite grant of opportunity, the appellant failed to lead evidence before the Reference Court.
As a result, there was no evidence on record to support the prayer for enhancement in the amount of compensation.
The Reference Court therefore, proceeded to dismiss the reference petition.
11. The land of the appellant having been acquired, it would be a statutory right to seek enhancement in the amount of compensation.

No doubt an opportunity was granted to the appellant to lead evidence Bharatkumar Vishnudas Bhutada Through ... vs The Executive Engineer, And Ors on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22724982/
4  ::: Uploaded on - 12/04/2024 ::: Downloaded on - 27/04/2024 15:2  ppn 5 53.wp-3870.23.doc but he failed to do so.

sentences.text: According to the appellant, his Power of Attorney holder did not discharge the responsibility that was expected to be discharged by him.
Be that as it may, we find that since the land of the appellant has been acquired, an opportunity deserves to be granted to him to seek enhancement in the amount of compensation.

However, at the same time while granting such opportunity, the Acquiring Body cannot be saddled with the liability to pay interest in case the amount of compensation is enhanced for the period during which the appellant was not diligent in prosecuting the reference proceedings.
The appellant cannot be permitted to take advantage of his absence before the Reference Court.

Hence while granting such opportunity to the appellant to lead evidence before the Reference Court, the interest of justice requires that the appellant be deprived of interest on the amount of compensation, if enhanced, for the period from 1 st January 2020 till today.

Further, the respondent no.1 being required to contest the present proceedings in this Court, the appellant ought to pay cost of Rs.20,000/- to respondent no.1 as a condition precedent for re-opening the proceedings before the Reference Court.
The point as framed is answered by holding that the appellant is entitled to an opportunity to lead evidence before the Reference Court subject to conditions referred to hereinabove.

sentences.text:
Hence for the aforesaid reasons, the following order is passed :-
 ORDER (i) The judgment dated 1st January 2020 passed by the learned Civil Judge, Senior Division, Solapur in Land Acquisition Reference No.74 of 2013 is set aside.
(ii) The proceedings are restored before the Reference Court for deciding the same afresh in accordance with law and after giving an opportunity to the parties.
(iii) In case the appellant is held entitled for enhancement in the amount of compensation, he would not be entitled to receive interest on the same for the period from 1 st January 2020 till today.
(iv) The reference proceedings shall be decided expeditiously on its own merits and in accordance with law.
(v) The appellant to pay cost of Rs.20,000/- to respondent no.1 as a condition precedent.
(vi) The record and proceedings be sent to the Reference Court forthwith.
13. The First Appeal is allowed in aforesaid terms with no order as to costs.

JITENDRA JAIN, J. A.S. CHANDURKAR, J.
